report.source_text: With the diagnosis of SVCS, the patient was directed for urgent chemotherapy with etoposide (120 mg daily given intravenously for 5 days) and cisplatin (70 mg given intravenously on the day one). The SVCS responded to treatment with complete reduction of upper body oedema and settling of respiratory distress within 5 days of treatment. The patient was started on spironolactone and intravenous KCl for hypokalaemia, ketoconazole for steroidogenesis inhibition and prophylactic antibiotics.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 56-year-old man presented with a 3-month history of worsening respiratory distress, proximal muscle weakness, hyperpigmentation, weight loss, apathy, facial swelling, and headache, with a significant smoking history. Initial CT scan revealed a lobulated solid soft-tissue mass (11.7x5.7x4.7 cm) in the right hilar region and severely stretched proximal superior vena cava with luminal narrowing, confirming Superior Vena Cava Syndrome (SVCS). A bronchial biopsy was performed, and its histological examination confirmed the diagnosis of Small Cell Lung Carcinoma (SCLC), further supported by strong positivity for chromogranin and synaptophysin on immunohistochemistry. Investigations for paraneoplastic syndromes showed raised 9-am serum cortisol and increased ACTH levels, with unsuppressed cortisol by dexamethasone, indicating ACTH-dependent hypercortisolism, consistent with ectopic ACTH secretion. The patient received urgent chemotherapy with etoposide and cisplatin for SVCS, which resulted in a complete reduction of upper body oedema and settling of respiratory distress within 5 days. Serum cortisol levels also significantly reduced from 1640 nmol/L to 213 nmol/L, indicating a good initial response to treatment. Supportive care included spironolactone, intravenous KCl, ketoconazole, and prophylactic antibiotics.
